title: Data Center Is Fined $1.1 Million for Operating 62 Power Generators

reading.body:
This is a compliance failure at the power layer of a data center build, not a failure of a model or a dataset. The generators that back the site were installed and run before the permits that New Jersey requires for either step existed, which means the facility was drawing on equipment that had never been through the state's air pollution review. The failure sits in the gap between construction and operation, where physical infrastructure was energised while the regulatory precondition for doing so was still unmet.

Catching it earlier would have taken a permitting check inside the operator's own build process, run before the generators were started rather than after. State inspectors found the unpermitted units during a site visit, so the detection came from outside the company. A pre-energisation compliance gate, or a construction-stage review that treated generator permits as a blocker rather than a follow-up, is the kind of control that would have surfaced the same fact before the equipment was in use.

What is not established is intent. The reporting describes a penalty for operating without permits and does not say whether the omission was deliberate. The federal lawsuit over noise is a filed claim, not a ruling, and the county violation orders are administrative actions. The reporting does not establish that the generators are the source of the noise the homeowners complain of.

reports.title: Data Center Is Fined $1.1 Million for Operating 62 Power Generators

summary:
New Jersey fined DataOne $1.07 million after state inspectors found 62 natural gas generators at its Vineland data center site in late July. The 2,000 kilowatt generators, each about the size of a tractor trailer, lacked required permits to be installed or operated. The penalty was for violating the state's Air Pollution Control Act and is the largest ever issued to a data center operator in New Jersey, officials said.

The Vineland campus is under construction and is planned to be a 2.6 million square foot complex needing 350 megawatts, with completion set for the end of the year. Some of it is already in use. Homeowners have filed a federal lawsuit over persistent noise, and the Cumberland County Health Department has issued violation orders to DataOne for excessive noise.
